🇲🇽🛢️ <u>Fuel Smuggling: 61,785 Million Pesos in Dodged Taxes</u>

Cross-checking data from 16 institutions, Mexico's government found 8,824 million liters of fuel in 2025 that didn't add up between what companies bought, moved, invoiced and sold — about 61,785 million pesos in unpaid IEPS tax, Energy Secretary Luz Elena González reported. Trading intermediaries account for 72% of the gaps, gas stations 13%. Sheinbaum now proposes limiting intermediation. The door was opened by Peña Nieto's 2013 energy reform, which handed fuel imports to private players with PRI and PAN votes.

🇲🇽🌧️ <u>Army and Navy Pull 41 People From Los Cabos Floodwaters</u>

Mexico's Defense and Navy ministries activated the DN-III-E and Plan Marina in Baja California Sur and Sonora after Cold Front No. 4 dumped intense rain on the northwest. In Los Cabos, troops rescued 41 people from high-risk areas and recovered 18 vehicles swept away by the currents. In Guaymas, Sonora, two people died when their vehicle was dragged off. Both plans are now in their recovery phase.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Cofece Saw the INE Printing Cartel in 2022 — and Did Nothing</u>

On July 7, 2022, Mexico's now-defunct competition watchdog Cofece flagged "indications of absolute monopolistic practices" in the printing of ballots and electoral materials: price manipulation, supply restriction, coordinated bids. Four years later, the INE's own comptroller found 5 companies and 13 people splitting 2,461 million pesos in contracts. When one winning supplier delivered late, the INE set the penalty at 26,000 pesos instead of 43 million. Analyst Ignacio Martínez Cortés of Lacen: "the commission worked through omissions."

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>Pemex and Petrobras Move to Close Joint Projects After Lula's Win</u>

Pemex expects to finalize joint exploration and production projects with Brazil's Petrobras in the "very short term," El Financiero reports. Octavio Barrera, Pemex's director of exploration and extraction, said the two companies are "sharing information to analyze in technical detail the areas of shared interest." They are reviewing eight seismic studies covering deepwater Gulf zones such as Máximo, Centauro and Holok-Alvarado, plus the mature Kayab and Pit fields.

🇲🇽🏛️ <u>Sheinbaum Proposes Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas for the Rotonda de las Personas Ilustres</u>

At the homage at Bellas Artes, President Sheinbaum announced that she had asked Interior Secretary Rosa Icela Rodríguez to start the process of moving Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas's remains to the Rotonda de las Personas Ilustres. Created in 1872, the Rotonda holds the people who shaped Mexico's history. Cárdenas's family accepted the proposal.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>94% of Corruption Complaints Stuck at the FGR's Anti-Corruption Unit</u>

Of the 1,300 criminal complaints the Anti-Corruption and Good Government Ministry says it has filed, only 80 have reached a judge, Miguel Badillo reports. That leaves 93.9% waiting. The cases sit with the FGR's Specialized Anti-Corruption Prosecutor's Office, which has been run by María de la Luz Mijangos since 2019.

One of them is the Agronitrogenados file: Pemex's purchase of a scrapped fertilizer plant, with an estimated 700 million dollars in damage to the public purse. Sheinbaum has publicly flagged it as stalled.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>At the G20 in Atlanta, Mexico Puts Sovereign Equality on the Table</u>

At the G20 foreign ministers' session on geopolitical tensions, hosted by Marco Rubio in Atlanta, Mexico's Foreign Minister Roberto Velasco set out the rule Mexico wants applied to everyone: "Under international law, all States are equal and subject to the same norms that govern their mutual relations." He said the sovereignty and territorial integrity of every State deserve respect, defended the T-MEC and Plan México as engines of stable jobs and better wages, and argued that the cost of global tensions must not fall on the poorest.

He said it the same week Texas claimed nine Mexican islands in the Río Bravo.

🇲🇽🌾 <u>Mexico's Rice Harvest Jumps 17.3%</u>

Mexico produced 257,480 tonnes of rice in 2025, up 17.3% from 219,587 in 2024, according to the Agriculture Ministry (Sader). The area planted grew 28.4%, from 31,346 to 40,250 hectares, and the value of the harvest rose 12.5% to 1.463 billion pesos. Nayarit led with 79,737 tonnes, followed by Campeche with 61,670 and Michoacán with 37,300.
